name: A. J. Swoboda
bio: Dr. A. J. Swoboda is an associate professor of Bible and theology at Bushnell University and co-host of the Slow Theology podcast. He specializes in Christian formation, spiritual disciplines, and contemporary theological issues, with a particular focus on practices like sabbath and doubt in the modern church.

name: Aimee Byrd
bio: Aimee Byrd is an author, speaker, and Bible study teacher who writes about theology, biblical womanhood, and evangelical culture. She is known for her theological depth and challenges to shallow women's ministry resources, and regularly contributes to Christianity Today.

books.title: Recovering from Biblical Manhood and Womanhood

name: Bethel McGrew
bio: Bethel McGrew is a freelance writer, educator, and mathematician whose essays on Christianity and culture appear in First Things, The Spectator, WORLD, and other national publications. She maintains the popular Further Up Substack newsletter.

name: Bonnie Kristian
bio: Bonnie Kristian is a deputy editor at Christianity Today who writes extensively on religion, faith, foreign policy, and Christian community. Her work bridges evangelical thought with mainstream journalism and she is the author of Untrustworthy and A Flexible Faith.

name: Campbell Markham
bio: Campbell Markham is a Presbyterian pastor in Tasmania who specializes in Reformation history and biblical languages. He is the Moderator of the Presbyterian Church of Tasmania and has published translations and historical works including a biography of Marie Durand.

books.title: Marie Durand, Prisoner of the Tour de Constance

name: Carey Nieuwhof
bio: Carey Nieuwhof is a bestselling leadership author, former attorney, and founding pastor of Connexus Church. His Carey Nieuwhof Leadership Podcast ranks in the top 0.1% of podcasts worldwide and he is a sought-after speaker on Christian leadership and sustainable ministry pace.
education: BA in Law; BA in Theology, University of Toronto

name: Clarissa Moll
bio: Clarissa Moll is an award-winning writer and podcaster specializing in grief and bereavement ministry. Her writing appears in Christianity Today and The Gospel Coalition, and she is the author of Beyond the Darkness, a guide for living and thriving after loss.

name: Daniel K. Williams
bio: Daniel K. Williams is a historian at Ashland University specializing in American religion and politics, the Christian Right, and the pro-life movement. His scholarly works examine the intersection of faith and American political history.

name: Danny Franks
bio: Danny Franks is the Pastor of Guest Services at The Summit Church in Durham, North Carolina, overseeing hospitality across ten campuses. He is an author and consultant helping churches welcome guests with gospel-centered hospitality.

name: David Mathis
bio: David Mathis is executive editor at Desiring God and pastor at Cities Church in Saint Paul. An author of numerous books and hundreds of articles, he blends pastoral ministry with theological teaching on joy, grace, and spiritual disciplines.

name: German Saucedo
bio: German Saucedo is a Mexican writer, lawyer, and cultural commentator based in New York. Associate Editor and Podcast Producer at First Things, he writes essays on theology, culture, and philosophy with a focus on faith and contemporary issues.

name: Greg Morse
bio: Greg Morse is a staff writer at Desiring God and a graduate of Bethlehem College and Seminary. A prolific author of essays on biblical theology and Christian living, his writing covers topics including biblical manhood, the new birth, and spiritual formation.

name: J. Gary Millar
bio: J. Gary Millar is the Principal of Queensland Theological College in Brisbane, Australia, and a theologian specializing in Old Testament and biblical theology. A former pastor in Ireland and Northern Ireland, he has particular expertise in Deuteronomy and the theology of prayer.

books.title: Calling on the Name of the Lord

name: Jemar Tisby
bio: Jemar Tisby is a New York Times bestselling historian, author, and speaker focusing on race, religion, and social movements. A professor at Simmons College of Kentucky, he is known for his scholarship on the American church's relationship with racism and justice.

name: Joy Marie Clarkson
bio: Joy Marie Clarkson is a writer, podcaster, and researcher at King's College London specializing in theology and literature. Books and Culture Editor at Plough Quarterly, she explores art, theology, and contemporary culture through her published works and popular podcast.

name: Kara Bettis Carvalho
bio: Kara Bettis Carvalho is a senior features editor at Christianity Today with over a decade of religion journalism experience. An award-winning reporter and storyteller, she covers faith, politics, and culture with a focus on long-form profiles and reported features.

name: Karen Swallow Prior
bio: Karen Swallow Prior is an award-winning author and scholar specializing in literature, ethics, and Christian thought. She writes extensively on faith, culture, and the integration of reading with spiritual formation, and is a fellow at the Trinity Forum.

name: Kate Shellnutt
bio: Kate Shellnutt is the Editorial Director of News at Christianity Today, with over fifteen years of religion journalism experience. Her award-winning work has appeared in major publications including The New York Times and The Washington Post.

name: Kyle Worley
bio: Kyle Worley is the lead pastor of Mosaic Church in Richardson, Texas, and co-host of the Knowing Faith podcast with J. T. English and Jen Wilkin. An author and teacher with over twenty years in ministry, he writes on union with Christ and the theological formation of local churches.

name: Laura Wifler
bio: Laura Wifler is a bestselling author of children's and adult books exploring the intersection of faith and everyday life. Co-founder of Risen Motherhood and founder of The KidLit Lab, she is a beloved voice for Christian mothers and aspiring writers.

books.title: Any Time, Any Place, Any Prayer

name: Leland Ryken
bio: Leland Ryken is Professor Emeritus of English at Wheaton College with over half a century of teaching experience. The author of nearly sixty books on biblical and literary topics, he served as literary stylist for the English Standard Version of the Bible.

books.title: The Word of God in English
How to Read the Bible as Literature

name: Matthew Lee Anderson
bio: Matthew Lee Anderson is an Associate Professor of Ethics and Theology in Baylor University's Honors College and founder of Mere Orthodoxy. He is the author of several books addressing Christian ethics and co-hosts the Mere Fidelity podcast on theology and culture.
education: DPhil in Christian Ethics, Oxford University

name: Matthew Loftus
bio: Matthew Loftus is a family physician practicing at a mission hospital in Kenya, where he also teaches. A regular columnist for Christianity Today, he is the inaugural recipient of the Michael J. Gerson Memorial Prize for Excellence in Writing on Faith and Public Life.

name: Nadya Williams
bio: Nadya Williams is a classicist and historian who left academia to write about ancient Christianity and classical literature from a Christian perspective. Books Editor at Mere Orthodoxy, she is the author of Cultural Christians in the Early Church and other works on the ancient world.

books.title: Cultural Christians in the Early Church
Mothers, Children, and the Body Politic

name: Nate Fischer
bio: Nate Fischer is Chairman of American Reformer and founder and CEO of New Founding, a venture firm focused on Christian-centered American revitalization. A Harvard Law graduate, he writes on evangelical leadership and Christian cultural engagement.
education: JD, Harvard Law School; BA, Calvin College

name: O. Alan Noble
bio: O. Alan Noble is an Associate Professor of English at Oklahoma Baptist University and co-founder and editor-in-chief of Christ and Pop Culture. He is the author of several books examining contemporary culture, technology, and what it means to be human in a distracted age.
affiliation: Oklahoma Baptist University, Christ and Pop Culture

name: Phylicia Masonheimer
bio: Phylicia Masonheimer is a bestselling author, Bible teacher, and podcast host who equips Christians with theological depth and biblical thinking. Her work addresses topics ranging from womanhood and sexuality to grief and spiritual formation, and she is a contributor to Focus on the Family.

name: R. Albert Mohler Jr.
bio: R. Albert Mohler Jr. is the ninth president of The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary and one of the leading intellectuals of the evangelical movement in America. A prolific author and podcaster, he addresses Christian worldview issues and theological controversies facing the contemporary church.
education: PhD in Systematic & Historical Theology, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary

name: Ryan Burge
bio: Ryan Burge is a political scientist and statistician at Washington University in St. Louis specializing in the study of religion's impact on American politics and society. His research on religious demographics and the rise of the religiously unaffiliated has shaped how evangelicals understand cultural change.
education: PhD in Political Science, Southern Illinois University

books.title: 20 Myths about Religion and Politics in America

name: Scot McKnight
bio: Scot McKnight is an acclaimed New Testament scholar and historian of early Christianity who has written over eighty books on the historical Jesus, Christian theology, and biblical interpretation. A leading voice in evangelical scholarship, his work has shaped conversations on scripture, the kingdom of God, and ecclesiology.

name: Scott Hubbard
bio: Scott Hubbard is a managing editor at Desiring God and pastor at All Peoples Church in Minneapolis. The author of over two hundred articles, he writes to deepen joy in God through Jesus, particularly for those navigating doubt and spiritual darkness.

name: Sean McDowell
bio: Sean McDowell is an associate professor of apologetics at Talbot School of Theology at Biola University. An accomplished author and speaker, he equips the church and the next generation to defend the Christian faith with intellectual rigor and cultural relevance.
affiliation: Biola University, Talbot School of Theology
education: PhD in Apologetics and Worldview Studies

name: Timothy Paul Jones
bio: Timothy Paul Jones is the C. Edwin Gheens Professor of Christian Family Ministry and Vice President for Doctoral Studies at The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary. An evangelical scholar of apologetics and family ministry, he has authored or co-authored over twenty books making complex theological topics accessible to general audiences.

name: Keegan Martin
bio: Keegan Martin is a staff writer at World Magazine, where he covers religion, politics, and culture from a Christian worldview perspective. His reporting spans evangelical news, cultural analysis, and issues at the intersection of faith and public life.

name: Jillian Parks
bio: Jillian Parks is a writer and critic whose work appears in First Things, where she explores literature, culture, and the life of faith. She brings a thoughtful Catholic and broadly Christian lens to questions of art, community, and the spiritual life.

name: Elise Brandon
bio: Elise Brandon is a writer for Christianity Today, contributing articles on theology, church life, and the Christian calendar. Her work draws readers into deeper reflection on Scripture and the historic practices of the Christian faith.

name: Kyle Tucker
bio: Kyle Tucker is a writer and researcher contributing to The Gospel Coalition, where his work focuses on apologetics, biblical history, and the intellectual defense of the Christian faith. He writes for readers who want rigorous engagement with theological and historical questions.

name: Courtney Doctor
bio: Courtney Doctor is a Bible teacher, author, and women's ministry director who writes for The Gospel Coalition. She is the author of From Garden to Glory: A Bible Study on the Bible's Story and In View of God's Mercies: The Story of Salvation in Romans. Her writing helps women anchor their lives in the grand narrative of Scripture.

name: Melissa Kruger
bio: Melissa Kruger serves as director of women's initiatives at The Gospel Coalition and is the author of several books including The Envy of Eve, Walking with God in the Season of Motherhood, and In All Things. A graduate of Reformed Theological Seminary, she writes with warmth and theological depth on discipleship, community, and the Christian life.
education: MA in Biblical Studies, Reformed Theological Seminary

books.title: Walking with God in the Season of Motherhood

name: Ginger Blomberg
bio: Ginger Blomberg is a writer for The Gospel Coalition who covers international Christianity, church growth, and mission. Her reporting brings attention to the global body of Christ, particularly stories of faith flourishing in places where the gospel is spreading rapidly.

name: John Taylor
bio: John Taylor is a writer contributing to Relevant Magazine on topics of faith, culture, and Christian living. He writes for a younger evangelical audience navigating questions of spirituality, church, and life in a post-Christian culture.

name: Alex Stevens
bio: Alex Stevens is a writer at Mere Orthodoxy, where he engages the intersection of classical Christian thought and contemporary culture. His essays draw on theological and philosophical tradition — including figures like Thomas Aquinas — to illuminate questions of education, virtue, and the common good.

name: Matthew Spear
bio: Matthew Spear is a writer for Relevant Magazine whose work explores the spiritual disciplines, Christian formation, and the life of faith in everyday culture. He writes with pastoral attentiveness to the challenges of faithful living in a distracted age.

name: Kelly M. Kapic
bio: Kelly M. Kapic is professor of theological studies at Covenant College and a widely read voice in evangelical theology. He is the author of You're Only Human: How Your Limits Reflect God's Design and Why That's Good, Embodied Hope: A Theological Meditation on Pain and Suffering, and numerous other works. His scholarship bridges systematic theology and spiritual formation, helping Christians embrace their creaturely limitations as gifts from God.
education: PhD in Theology, King's College London

name: M. Elizabeth Lewis Hall
bio: M. Elizabeth Lewis Hall is a professor of psychology at Rosemead School of Psychology at Biola University, where she researches the integration of Christian theology and psychological science. Her scholarly and popular writing addresses human embodiment, suffering, and what it means to be made in the image of God.
affiliation: Biola University / Rosemead School of Psychology

name: Jason McMartin
bio: Jason McMartin is a professor of theology at Rosemead School of Psychology at Biola University, where he works at the intersection of systematic theology and the behavioral sciences. His writing explores Christian anthropology, sanctification, and the theological dimensions of human flourishing.
affiliation: Biola University / Rosemead School of Psychology

books.title: Being Saved: Dimensions of Human Salvation

name: Jamie Carlson
bio: Jamie Carlson is a writer at Mere Orthodoxy who engages questions of gender, theology, and evangelical culture with careful attention to both Scripture and tradition. Her essays call for more substantive theological engagement in evangelical debates that are often reduced to political or cultural terms.

name: William Tate
bio: William Tate is a writer at Mere Orthodoxy contributing essays on literature, culture, and the Christian intellectual tradition. He writes with an eye toward recovering the richness of Christian humanist thought for evangelical readers navigating questions of art, education, and the good life.

name: Joshua Mitchell
bio: Joshua Mitchell is a professor of political theory at Georgetown University and the author of American Awakening: Identity Politics and Other Afflictions of Our Time. He writes at the intersection of Christian theology and political philosophy, bringing a Tocquevillian lens to contemporary cultural and spiritual debates.

name: James Norris
bio: James Norris is a writer and pastor contributing to Reformation21, the online journal of the Alliance of Confessing Evangelicals. He writes on biblical exegesis, Reformed theology, and the church's witness in a post-Christian culture.

name: Josh Burnett
bio: Josh Burnett is a writer and ministry practitioner contributing to the Carey Nieuwhof platform, where he addresses church leadership, preaching, and ministry strategy. His work helps pastors think through the practical and theological dimensions of sermon preparation and congregational discipleship.

name: Nick Batzig
bio: Nick Batzig is a contributing editor at Ligonier Ministries and serves as pastor of New Covenant Presbyterian Church (PCA) in Richmond Hill, Georgia. A thoughtful expositor and Reformed theologian, he writes on covenant theology, biblical typology, and the doctrines of grace.

name: Tim Rosenberger
bio: Tim Rosenberger is a writer at Mere Orthodoxy who explores the relationship between authentic faith and the cultural forces that can distort it. His essays examine how sentiment, aesthetics, and cultural Christianity can substitute for genuine conviction, calling evangelicals back to a more robust theological and spiritual foundation.

name: Sara Lansford
bio: Sara Lansford is a writer and researcher with Lifeway Research, contributing to evangelical conversations about children's ministry, faith formation, and reaching the next generation. Her work draws on research data to help churches and parents think strategically about passing faith to children.

name: Nathaniel Marshall
bio: Nathaniel Marshall is a writer and book reviewer at Mere Orthodoxy who engages Christian intellectual culture through careful reading and criticism. His reviews and essays take seriously both ideas and the books that carry them, serving readers who want substantive engagement with the evangelical and broader Christian mind.

name: Angela Fulton
bio: Angela Fulton is a writer for Christianity Today who covers global Christianity, the church in conflict zones, and the lives of Christians navigating faith under pressure. Her reporting brings American evangelical readers into contact with the worldwide body of Christ.

name: Ryan Smith
bio: Ryan Smith is a writer for American Reformer contributing to evangelical conversations about education, culture, and Christian citizenship. His work engages the classical Christian education movement and broader questions of how Christians should form the next generation.

name: Todd Boone
bio: Todd Boone is a pastor and writer contributing to Reformation21, the online journal of the Alliance of Confessing Evangelicals. He writes on biblical exposition, Reformed theology, and the spiritual significance of the church calendar and ordinances.

name: Mike Sabo
bio: Mike Sabo is a writer and editor at American Reformer, where he covers conservative Christian politics, cultural analysis, and the challenges facing the church in American public life. He writes from a Reformed perspective on nationalism, the common good, and Christian civic engagement.

name: John W. Hoyum
bio: John W. Hoyum is a pastor and writer at American Reformer who addresses the economic and institutional challenges facing the pastoral ministry. He advocates for fair compensation of clergy and writes on the health of the local church as an institution within broader society.

name: James Abernathy
bio: James Abernathy is a writer for The Gospel Coalition whose work engages disability theology, embodiment, and the full inclusion of people with disabilities in the life of the church. He writes with personal insight and theological care about what it means to bear the image of God in all its diversity.

name: Adam Griffin
bio: Adam Griffin is a pastor and writer for The Gospel Coalition whose work focuses on marriage, family discipleship, and the spiritual formation of the home. He helps parents and spouses think through how the gospel reshapes their most intimate relationships and responsibilities.

name: Benjamin L. Gladd
bio: Benjamin L. Gladd is associate professor of New Testament at Reformed Theological Seminary in Jackson, Mississippi. He is the co-author of Making All Things New: Inaugurated Eschatology for the Life of the Church and contributes to The Gospel Coalition on biblical theology, eschatology, and the redemptive-historical reading of Scripture.
affiliation: Reformed Theological Seminary / The Gospel Coalition
education: PhD in New Testament, Wheaton College

name: Sidney Dyer
bio: Sidney Dyer is a writer and editor contributing to Ligonier Ministries, where he explores Reformed theology, the doctrine of God, and topics in systematic and biblical theology. His work serves readers seeking rigorous engagement with the classic doctrines of the Christian faith.

name: Kirsten Sanders
bio: Kirsten Sanders is a writer at Mere Orthodoxy who engages questions of art, culture, and Christian faithfulness. Her essays examine how Christians should navigate contested cultural spaces — including film, visual art, and public discourse — with discernment and conviction.

name: Nate Shurden
bio: Nate Shurden is a writer for Ligonier Ministries who contributes expositions of Scripture and meditations on the life of Christ for evangelical readers. His work draws on careful biblical study to illuminate the meaning and significance of the gospel narratives.

name: Gene Edward Veith
bio: Gene Edward Veith Jr. is professor of literature at Patrick Henry College and a contributing editor at World Magazine and Ligonier Ministries. One of evangelical Christianity's leading voices on culture and the arts, he is the author of numerous books including Postmodern Times, State of the Arts, and God at Work: Your Christian Vocation in All of Life. He writes from a confessional Lutheran perspective on everything from classical education to contemporary media.
affiliation: Patrick Henry College / World Magazine / Ligonier Ministries
education: PhD in English, University of Kansas

name: Christopher Gehrz
bio: Christopher Gehrz is professor of history at Bethel University in St. Paul, Minnesota, and the author of The Pietist Vision of Christian Higher Education. He blogs at The Pietist Schoolman and writes on church history, the Pietist tradition, and the relationship between faith and scholarship. His work at Mere Orthodoxy brings a historian's perspective to evangelical self-understanding.

books.title: The Pietist Vision of Christian Higher Education

name: Brittany Dahl
bio: Brittany Dahl is a writer for The Gospel Coalition whose work draws on literature, imagination, and the Christian tradition to illuminate the gospel. She writes on how stories — from C.S. Lewis's Narnia to Scripture itself — can form our affections and deepen our love for Christ.

name: Ian J. Vaillancourt
bio: Ian J. Vaillancourt is a biblical scholar and writer for The Gospel Coalition who specializes in Old Testament wisdom literature. His work explores how the Psalms, Proverbs, and the wisdom books of Scripture speak to the full range of human experience and point readers toward Christ.

name: Annie Eisner
bio: Annie Eisner is a writer for Relevant Magazine who addresses theology, relationships, and the Christian life for a younger evangelical audience. She brings a pastoral and culturally engaged voice to questions of biblical sexuality, marriage, and how Christians navigate contemporary life with conviction.
